summary: North Macedonia grants 90 visa-free days to citizens of the EU, UK, US, most of the Americas and its Balkan neighbours, while visa-required nationalities can either apply at an embassy or enter for up to 15 days per visit on a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa.

conditionalWaivers.text: Holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen (type C) visa, valid at least five days beyond the intended stay, may enter North Macedonia without a visa for up to 15 days per visit — confirm current terms with a North Macedonian embassy before travel.

fee.notes: Commonly cited fee — confirm the current amount with the North Macedonian embassy handling your application.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned stay in North Macedonia — keep a comfortable margin and confirm with the embassy if your passport is close to expiry.

travelInsurance.text: Not a condition of entry for visa-free visitors, though visa applicants must show travel health insurance. EU EHIC cards are not valid in North Macedonia, so private cover is strongly recommended.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of North Macedonia

onwardTicket.text: Not routinely checked, but border officers may ask about return plans, accommodation and sufficient means for the stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of North Macedonia

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published for tourists; border officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for their stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of North Macedonia

declarations.name: Registration of foreigners
declarations.text: Foreign visitors must be registered with the police within 48 hours of arrival. Hotels and registered guesthouses do this automatically; if you stay privately, your host must register you at the local police station. Unregistered stays can cause fines or problems on departure.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of North Macedonia

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared on entry and exit; taking larger undeclared sums out of the country can lead to confiscation.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of North Macedonia

payments.text: Cards are accepted in city hotels, supermarkets and bigger restaurants, but taxis, bazaars and rural guesthouses run on cash — pay in denars; euros are sometimes quoted but the change is poor.

safety.text: North Macedonia is generally safe, with little crime affecting tourists beyond occasional pickpocketing in Skopje. Drive defensively — road conditions and driving standards vary outside the main highways.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — North Macedonia Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: May–June and September–October are ideal for Skopje, Matka Canyon and hiking; July–August is hot but is peak season on Lake Ohrid.

idp.text: North Macedonia is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognise is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: North Macedonia is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognise is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national licence, and for how long a foreign licence may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for North Macedonia yet.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties

tips.text: You must be registered with the police within 48 hours of arrival — hotels handle it automatically; if you stay in a private apartment, make sure your host registers you and keep the confirmation.
Pay in denars (MKD) — cards work in cities, but taxis, markets and villages want cash, and prices quoted in euros usually build in a bad exchange rate.
Lake Ohrid is the summer highlight — July and August are busiest; June and September still have warm water, cheaper rooms and far fewer crowds.
Skopje suffers some of Europe's worst winter air pollution (roughly November–February) — travellers with respiratory conditions should check air-quality forecasts and plan accordingly.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for North Macedonia?
faq.answer: Most Western travellers don't: citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and most of the Americas can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period visa-free. Nationalities that need a visa can apply at a North Macedonian embassy — or enter for up to 15 days per visit if they hold a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa.

faq.question: Can I enter North Macedonia with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes — holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen (type C) visa can enter without a North Macedonian visa and stay up to 15 days per visit, provided the Schengen visa remains valid at least five days beyond the stay. Confirm the current terms with an embassy before travel.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in North Macedonia?
faq.answer: US passport holders can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period without a visa. North Macedonia is outside the Schengen Area, so this does not use up any of your Schengen days.

faq.question: What currency is used in North Macedonia?
faq.answer: The Macedonian denar (MKD). Cards are fine in cities, but carry denar cash for taxis, bazaars and the countryside — euros are sometimes accepted informally at poor rates.

faq.question: Can EU citizens enter North Macedonia with just an ID card?
faq.answer: EU citizens can enter with a valid biometric national ID card for short visits of up to 15 days; for longer stays (up to the full 90 days) travel with a passport.
